text: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) grants you access to some government records for a fee. 1 Before you request Information you seek may already be online. First determine if you need to make a request. 2 Make a request Make your request. To reduce processing time and fees, limit the scope of your request. 3 Track your request Determine where your FOIA request is. Consequently, the whistleblower data no longer includes a "Region" column. × Whistleblower Office Reports Red Team National Office Report Red Team Regional Offices Report - Part 1 Red Team Regional Offices Report - Part 2 Tiger Team Report × Archived Documents Accord Regarding BNSF Railway Company Policies COVID-19 Complaint Data Notice to Employees - JP Morgan Chase Previous Years Information Frequently Requested Under FOIA Secretary' Findings - JP Morgan Chase Whistleblower Office Reports × Before you request First, use OSHA's search box at the top of your screen to see if the information you seek is already publicly available. For Inspection Data Search the text of investigation summaries resulting from OSHA accident inspections. Search and locate OSHA enforcement inspections by a specific inspection number or within a specific industry NAICS or SIC . Find details from one or more inspections when the Activity numbers are known. Can't find it? View our Inspection Information Search help . Learn how to access citations issued to employers. For Work-Related Fatalities Explore data on work-related fatalities that occurred under Federal OSHA and State Plan jurisdiction for cases that have been closed or citations issued on or after January 1, 2017. Find archived fatality data for FY 2009 - FY 2017 summaries of work-related fatalities and incidents resulting in the hospitalization of three or more workers reported to Federal and State OSHA. For Establishment-Specific Injury and Illness Data Explore our Injury Tracking Application (ITA) data to download injury and illness data submitted by employers. OSHA has electronically collected OSHA Form 300A Summary of Injuries and Illnesses since 2016. In 2023, OSHA began collecting case detail data as recorded in OSHA Form 300 and 301. Search work-related injury and illness data before 2016 through the OSHA Data Initiative from establishments within specific industries and employment size from 1996 through 2011. For Severe Injury Reports (SIRs) Explore our Severe Injury Reports to review and download reports on severe injuries, defined as work-related in-patient hospitalizations, amputations, and eye losses, that were reported by employers from states covered by federal OSHA. OSHA has made this data publicly available for all SIRs reported to OSHA from establishments covered by federal OSHA since 2015. Take me to the Severe Injury Dashboard . Other Go to OSHA's Data page to view available data for download or visit the Department of Labor Data Catalog to download inspection data, citations, and violations data since 1970. Contact OSHA's Office of Communications at 202-693-1999 if you are a member of the media and have a question for OSHA. × Make a request: information needed to simplify your request If the employer is located in a state under federal OSHA jurisdiction , send an email to foiarequests@dol.gov , with the following information if you are seeking inspection records. Inspection number ( find it through inspections search ) City and state where incident occurred Date incident occurred Employer name that was inspected Your name (the requester) and your physical address. Choose only what is needed. In your email, let us know what records you want: OSHA-1. OSHA Inspection Report/Violation Worksheet (Formerly OSHA-1B Worksheet) Safety Narrative. Inspection Report (Formerly OSHA – 1A, Inspection Narrative Report) Violation Worksheet Citations Settlement Agreement Management or Managerial witness statements We encourage you to remove any request for records that are potentially: 1) commercial or financial; 2) confidential or privileged; and 3) received from a business. These records must go through Executive Order 12600 review, which increases the processing time. If you don’t need these records, add the following language to your request: I am not requesting any records subject to Executive Order 12600 . If the employer is not under federal OSHA, send your request to the state plan . Contact us if you have a question about your FOIA request. × Determine where your FOIA request is Step 1 : Check the status of your request If your request is closed, run a search in your e-mail inbox and spam folder for the FOIA closing letter from an e-mail with this address: @dol.gov or from secure.transfer@dol.gov . Step 2 : If your FOIA request is closed and you did not receive a FOIA closing letter or your request is still "Assigned for Processing" in Step 1, contact your local OSHA area office directly and ask for the OSHA FOIA officer. Step 3 : if your FOIA request is with the national OSHA office or you have questions, contact OSHA.FOIA@dol.gov .
